summary: Entering the Ruminant Feed Market with Launch of Tru Value Cattle Feed Range style bg-dark-grey We have entered the ruminant nutrition market with the launch of our Tru Value cattle feed range, marking a significant expansion of our Integrated Feed & Protein (IFP) business. The launch broadens our feed portfolio beyond poultry and aquaculture, strengthening our position as a provider of nutrition solutions across key livestock sectors. oga-container--news-detail-container no-spacer true true Tru Value was launched at an event in Nigeria, where we already have a strong presence in poultry and aquaculture feed production. The country is one of Africa’s largest livestock markets, with rising demand for animal protein and ongoing efforts to improve herd productivity, creating new opportunities for commercial cattle farming. The launch event in Kaduna State was attended by the Honourable Minister of Livestock Development, Alhaji Idi Mukhtar Maiha as well as government officials, commercial farmers, livestock industry stakeholders, development partners, distributors and members of the media. image articleImg middle landscape no-spacer oga-container--inner Our entry into ruminant nutrition marks an important milestone in the evolution of Olam Agri's feed business. We have built strong capabilities serving poultry and aquaculture farmers, and we are now extending that expertise to support the development of more productive and sustainable cattle farming systems. Nigeria is the first market for this expansion, and we see significant opportunities to help livestock farmers improve performance, strengthen food security and create greater value across the beef and dairy value chains. Sharad Gupta, President & Global Head, Integrated Feed & Protein, Olam Agri true right oga-container--inner The transformation of Nigeria's livestock sector begins with improving productivity at farm level. Quality animal nutrition remains one of the most important factors in achieving better growth rates, improved milk yields, and higher returns for our farmers. We commend Olam Agri for investing in innovative feed solutions that support the Federal Government's commitment to building a modern, competitive, and sustainable livestock industry. Partnerships like this are critical to enhancing food security, increasing farmer incomes, and accelerating economic growth. Alhaji Idi Mukhtar Maiha, Honourable Minister of Livestock Development, Nigeria true right The Minister added that the government would continue working to create an environment that attracts private sector investment and innovation across the livestock value chain. The Tru Value range includes three products. Tru Value Beef Pellet supports efficient weight gain and shorter fattening cycles. Tru Value Beef Plus Pellet is formulated for accelerated growth and superior finishing performance. Tru Value Dairy Pellet is designed to raise milk yield and overall herd productivity. All three come from extensive research and nutritional development work and are made to deliver the same balanced nutrition in every bag, every time addressing two of the most persistent frustrations farmers report with traditional feeding methods: inconsistency and unreliable supply. Several farmers at the event described what structured feeding had done for their own herds compared with conventional methods, offering the room a practical counterpoint to the technical presentations. Through our entry into ruminant nutrition, we are expanding our ability to serve livestock producers with science-based nutrition solutions across multiple species. The Tru Value launch in Nigeria represents the first step in the company's broader ambition to support more productive, sustainable and commercially viable livestock systems through nutrition, technical expertise and strategic partnerships. oga-container--news-detail-container no-spacer true true oga-button--align-center-lg oga-button--align-center-sm oga-inner oga-button--bottom-spacer,oga-button--top-spacer btn Subscribe to Our Newsletter redirect https://mailchi.mp/2bf931f9270f/olam-agri-newsletter-signup-form true btn Find Out More About Our Nigeria redirect /content/olamagri/gb/en/locations/nigeria true no-top-spacer /content/olamagri/gb/en/fragments/latest-news

Cookie Settings Accept All Press Release Energy & Maritime Solutions Hanwha Power receives ABS Approval in Principle for 1,700 TEU battery-powered container ship design October 23, 2026 Subscribe 00:00 00:00 Linkedin X Facebook URL Copy • Fully electric propulsion design featuring approximately 151 MWh of energy storage strengthens capabilities in zero-carbon maritime transport • Integrated solution combines electric propulsion and containerized battery energy storage systems • Expanded eco-friendly marine propulsion portfolio lays the groundwork for entry into the next-generation zero-carbon vessel market Hanwha Power received Approval in Principle (AiP) from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) for its 1,700 TEU battery-powered container ship design Hanwha Power announced on October 23 that it had received Approval in Principle (AiP) from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) for its design of a 1,700 TEU battery-powered container ship. The certificate presentation ceremony took place on October 22, local time, at the 2026 Maritime Hybrid, Electric & Hydrogen Fuel Cells Conference in Bergen, Norway. Jong-kyu Hwang, Vice President of Technology Solutions at Hanwha Power, attended the ceremony alongside senior representatives from ABS. The event runs from October 21 to 23 at Scandic Bergen City. The newly approved design concept features a fully electric container vessel powered by a large-scale 151 MWh energy storage system (ESS). Electrical energy stored in containerized battery units serves as the vessel’s primary propulsion source, enabling operation without direct carbon emissions through the use of port charging infrastructure. The use of containerized batteries, which can be handled and stowed like standard cargo containers, enhances space efficiency, maximizes cargo capacity, and optimizes overall vessel performance. This approach also supports flexible battery replacement and scalable operation, offering a practical pathway for the decarbonization of short-sea and regional container transport. The AiP strengthens Hanwha Power’s capabilities in fully electric vessel design using large-scale battery energy storage and expands its portfolio of marine propulsion solutions. The company plans to build on this achievement to pursue opportunities in the next-generation zero-carbon maritime transport market. Alongside the approval, Hanwha Power has also completed the basic design for a 1,000 TEU battery-powered container vessel. Building on its expertise in vessel design across multiple ship classes, the company aims to develop a comprehensive lineup of electric-propulsion vessels tailored to a wide range of operating conditions and customer needs. “This AiP from ABS marks an important step in extending Hanwha Power’s marine technology capabilities to fully electric vessels powered by large-scale battery systems,” said Jong-kyu Hwang, Vice President of Technology Solutions at Hanwha Power. “We will address the needs of the next-generation zero-carbon maritime transport market with integrated solutions that combine electric propulsion and containerized battery system technologies.” About Hanwha Power Hanwha Power is a specialized provider of energy equipment and eco-friendly solutions. Since establishing its Marine Solution Business Division in 2023, the company has been actively pursuing projects involving vessel retrofits, alternative-fuel propulsion, and energy-efficiency improvements. Hanwha Power provides differentiated eco-friendly marine solutions to global shipping companies, including vessel retrofits, onboard regasification and re-liquefaction systems, increased cargo containment capacity, and alternative-fuel conversions. Through these solutions, the company is leading the transition toward more sustainable marine transportation. title: 23 Oct 2026 · Press release Wärtsilä and WinGD sign new Service Framework Agreement to ensure long-term continuity and support for the global fleet
summary: Home Media Wärtsilä and WinGD sign new Service Framework Agreement to ensure long-term continuity and support for the global fleet Wärtsilä and WinGD sign new Service Framework Agreement to ensure long-term continuity and support for the global fleet Wärtsilä Corporation, Press release 23 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC+2 Technology groups Wärtsilä and WinGD have entered into a new long-term Service Framework Agreement, reaffirming their shared commitment to supporting shipowners and operators worldwide. Building on a collaboration that has been in place since 2015, the agreement confirms Wärtsilä's continued role as an authorised global service provider for WinGD, Wärtsilä and Sulzer-branded two-stroke engines. Customers worldwide now benefit from flexibility and choice in their service provider with WinGD and Wärtsilä both offering global expertise and support capabilities to help shipowners and operators maximise uptime, optimise maintenance planning, and prepare their fleets for future fuels, evolving technologies and decarbonisation requirements. “Our promise to customers is trusted, responsive and reliable support throughout the complete lifecycle of their engines; anytime, anywhere,” says Dominik Schneiter, CEO, WinGD. “This new Service Framework Agreement with Wärtsilä complements our own service offer, Global Service by WinGD, ensuring uninterrupted global support while giving customers access to the best available expertise for each engine generation. By combining the right capabilities where they add most value, the agreement provides a strong and flexible service solution for WinGD’s diverse global customer and product base." "This agreement confirms the continuity of a long-standing service relationship that has supported WinGD's installed base for over a decade," adds Roger Holm, President of Wärtsilä Marine & Executive Vice President at Wärtsilä Corporation. "It ensures that shipowners and operators continue to have access to Wärtsilä's global service network, technical expertise and lifecycle support, including long-term lifecycle agreements, for their two-stroke engines." WinGD was formed in 2015 when Wärtsilä sold its two-stroke engine business to China State Shipbuilding Corporation (CSSC). WinGD remains the OEM technology leader supporting its customers as a global service provider and licensor for all two-stroke engines under the WinGD, Wärtsilä and Sulzer names. Wärtsilä continues to offer genuine spare parts, field service, workshop capabilities, technical support, long-term agreements and decades of installed-base experience. The Service Framework Agreement reflects the long-term relationship between the companies and provides customers with confidence that expert, authorised support will remain available throughout the operating life of their engines. Media contact for more information on this release: Isabella Alder, External Communications, Wärtsilä Marine [email protected] Image caption: Wärtsilä and WinGD have signed a new Service Framework Agreement, reaffirming their shared commitment to supporting shipowners and operators worldwide (Left to right: Dominik Schneiter, CEO, WinGD, Peter Knaapen, Director, 2-stroke Services, Wärtsilä Marine) © Wärtsilä Corporation All Wärtsilä releases are available at www.wartsila.com/media/news-releases and at news.cision.com/wartsila-corporation where also the images can be downloaded. Use of the image(s) is allowed only in connection with the contents of this press release. Wärtsilä images are available at www.wartsila.com/media/image-bank . Wärtsilä Marine in brief Wärtsilä Marine is a global pioneer in power, propulsion and lifecycle solutions for the marine market. We develop industry-leading technologies, advancing maritime's transition to new fuels. We support building an end-to-end digital ecosystem where all vessels and ports are connected. Ultimately, Wärtsilä Marine is driving the shipping industry forward on its journey towards a decarbonised and sustainable future through our broad portfolio of engines, propulsion systems, hybrid technology, exhaust treatment, shaft line solutions and digital technologies, as well as integrated powertrain systems. Our offering, which is underpinned by our performance-based agreements, upgrades, lifecycle solutions, decarbonisation services, as well as an unrivalled global network of maritime expertise, delivers the efficiency, reliability, safety, and environmental performance needed to support a safe and sustainable future for our customers, our communities and our planet. www.wartsila.com/marine Wärtsilä in brief Wärtsilä is a global leader in innovative technologies and lifecycle solutions for the marine and energy industries. We emphasise innovation in sustainable technology and services to help our customers continuously improve environmental and economic performance. Our dedicated and passionate team of 17,900 professionals in 199 locations in 78 countries shape the decarbonisation transformation of our industries across the globe. In 2025, Wärtsilä’s net sales totalled EUR 6.9 billion. Wärtsilä is listed on Nasdaq Helsinki. www.wartsila.com WinGD in brief WinGD advances the decarbonisation of marine transportation through sustainable energy systems using the most advanced technologies in emissions reduction, fuel efficiency, hybridisation and digital optimisation. With their two-stroke low-speed engines at the heart of the power equation, WinGD sets the industry standard for reliability, safety, efficiency, and environmental design - supported by Global Service by WinGD, which delivers tailored 24X7 lifecycle engine support through Swiss engineering excellence, dependable maintenance, rapid global response, and genuine parts to keep engines performing at their best. Headquartered in Winterthur, Switzerland since its origin as the Sulzer Diesel Engine business in 1893, today it is powering the transformation to a sustainable future. title: POWERGRID Commissions Project to Evacuate Renewable Energy in Karnataka
summary: Power Grid Corporation of India (POWERGRID) has commissioned a transmission project to evacuate renewable energy in Koppal and Gadag, Karnataka. The ‘Transmission Scheme for integration of Renewable Energy Zone (Phase-II) in Koppal-II (Phase-A & B) and Gadag-II (Phase- A)’ was commissioned on October 23, 2026. It was entrusted to POWERGRID Koppal Gadag Transmission, a subsidiary of POWERGRID, which was amalgamated with POWERGRID Khavda II-C Transmission on March 1, 2026.

title: Fourth Partner Energy Secures ₹7.5 Billion to Finance Wind-Solar Project
summary: Renewable energy solutions company Fourth Partner Energy (FPEL) has raised ₹7.5 billion (~$79.27 million) from Tata Capital – Cleantech Finance (TCCL) to develop its ongoing solar-plus-wind project with an integrated battery energy storage system in Maharashtra. The project comprises 300 MW of solar capacity, 50 MW of wind capacity and 750 MWh of battery energy storage. It is expected to generate more than 630 million units of clean power annually for the company’s corporate consumers in Maharashtra.
